## Why wrangling matters (30 seconds)

Raw experiment tables are almost never analysis-ready.

- Columns may be wide, messy, or split across files
- We need a clean table: one row per observation, clear columns for predictors/outcomes

**`dplyr`** is how we reshape and filter those tables so plots and models can run.

Keep a before/after picture in mind: messy spreadsheet → tidy analysis table.

## Slide conventions

- Use code formatting for special terms and examples, such as `This` or **`This are code`**.

- Code chunk, and it is executable when you open the file in RStudio
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
# Title: Example code chunk
# This chunk shows the basic structure of an executable R block.
```

- `.qmd` version file won't have the image display but the content is the same
